\noindent\textit{Sheltered Bidding: The Within-Auction Cost of SME Set-Asides}

\bigskip

\begin{itemize}
\item SME-only set-aside imposes R\$\,\welfAnnualBRLLo~M (US\$\,\welfAnnualUSDLo~M) per year in welfare loss on S\~ao Paulo's medical-supplies procurement at the observed \adherenceGsixtyfivePost\% adherence rate---R\$\,\welfRangeLoBRL--\welfRangeHiBRL~M across the realistic adherence range of \welfAdherenceLoPct--\welfAdherenceHiPct\%.
\item Roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of the cost is sheltered bidding within the auction, not entry-margin reshuffling.
\item Endogenous SME entry is a partial offset that attenuates a \latentShockRatioNp\% larger latent within-auction shock in non-pharma and a \latentShockRatioPh\% larger one in pharma.
\item DiD against \controlGroupCount{} never-treated controls: \didLowerPct--\didUpperPct\% rise in winning prices; SME participation roughly doubles.
\item A \optPrefThreshold{} SME price preference welfare-dominates the set-aside in thick standardized markets at near-zero fiscal cost.
\item The \emph{empate ficto} right-to-match (\LCSmeStatute{} arts.~44--45) operative in current Brazilian law sits below the price preference on both distributive and welfare margins: \(\sim\)\vFourSmeWinGainPh--\vFourSmeWinGainNp{}~pp SME win-rate gain at essentially zero welfare cost.
\end{itemize}
